question: What does the WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted in May 2025 commit countries to?
text:
The WHO Pandemic Agreement, adopted by the World Health Assembly on **May 20, 2025**, sets out what countries that become parties will do to **prevent pandemics, prepare for them, and respond together**. A central goal is to make vaccines, tests, and treatments available according to public-health need, not just countries’ ability to pay. ([apps.who.int](https://apps.who.int/gb/ebwha/pdf_files/WHA78/A78_R1-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Its main commitments are to:

- **Strengthen prevention and preparedness.** Improve disease surveillance and early warning, maintain national preparedness plans, and build resilient health systems and a trained health workforce. The agreement calls for a *One Health* approach, which recognizes the links between human, animal, and environmental health. ([apps.who.int](https://apps.who.int/gb/ebwha/pdf_files/WHA78/A78_R1-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Make pandemic supplies more accessible.** Cooperate on research and development, expand manufacturing across regions, promote technology transfer, and coordinate procurement and distribution through a global supply-chain network. ([apps.who.int](https://apps.who.int/gb/ebwha/pdf_files/WHA78/A78_R1-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Share information and the benefits it helps produce.** The agreement provides for a Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system that pairs rapid sharing of pathogen samples and genetic sequence data with equitable access to resulting vaccines, tests, and treatments. During a pandemic emergency, participating manufacturers would aim to make **20% of their real-time production** of relevant products available to WHO for allocation based on public-health need. That target applies to participating manufacturers, not to each country’s stockpile. ([apps.who.int](https://apps.who.int/gb/ebwha/pdf_files/WHA78/A78_R1-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Cooperate on financing and implementation.** Support preparedness and response at home and internationally, including through a financing mechanism intended to help countries with fewer resources build capacity. ([apps.who.int](https://apps.who.int/gb/ebwha/pdf_files/WHA78/A78_R1-en.pdf))

**Adoption did not make the agreement binding.** As of November 24, 2026, the benefit-sharing annex was still under negotiation, with countries aiming to bring it to the World Health Assembly in **May 2027**. The agreement opens for signature after the annex is adopted and enters into force 30 days after the 60th ratification. It does **not** give WHO authority to impose lockdowns, vaccine mandates, or travel restrictions. ([who.int](https://www.who.int/news/item/13-11-2026-member-states-reiterate-commitment-to-finalize-pandemic-agreement-pabs-annex-by-may-2027?utm_source=openai))
